## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop. Session chip leader despite exploitable tendencies — volume/aggression accumulates chips.** 3-bets extremely wide — includes mid pocket pairs and trash. Calls down with virtually anything (overcards, bottom pair). **Postflop as PFA**: (1) **Air line**: c-bets flop then checks/folds turn when called — profitable float spot. (2) **Medium-strength line**: checks flop then bets turn = real hand (delayed value). **As caller**: Will call all three streets with marginal holdings. **Exploit**: 3-bet for value. Value bet EXTREMELY thin. Do NOT bluff. Float flop c-bets when P2 is PFA. Fold ace-high to check-flop/bet-turn line. Despite being exploitable per-hand, respect that their aggression generates chips — don't donate to their volume.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, skilled. Consistent winner — second in chips.** Opens and 4-bets wider than premium (suited aces as semi-bluffs). Actively 3-bets from SB vs late-position steals. **Postflop**: Checks draws on flop, leads turn when completing. **Confirmed trapper** — check-calls multiple streets with two pair+. River checks can be traps after passive lines. Folds dry boards without connections. **Exploit**: C-bet dry boards. Turn leads after flop checks = completed draw. Don't value-bet thin on river. Can call wider vs 4-bets. Tighten steals when P3 in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~47%), passive preflop, historically #1 chip accumulator.** Limps weak, raises better. 3-bets 99+, shoves AA. **Limp-reraise = strong (99+).** EXTREMELY sticky — calls river with 9-high and bottom pair. Strong hands: check-raises AND donk-bets. Aggressive postflop when holding strong hands. **Exploit**: Isolate limps with position. Value bet EXTREMELY wide — #1 value target. NEVER bluff. Respect check-raises, donk-bets, and limp-reraises.

**Player 5**: **Nit (~8-10% VPIP) but effective.** Any preflop raise = strong hand. **Four postflop lines**: (1) Single donk-bet (made hand) but folds to raises/turn barrels — exploit with two-barrel bluffs. (2) Donk-bet + shove = strong draw. (3) Multi-street barreling = nutted range (AK/sets) — FOLD without the nuts. (4) Passive calling = weaker range, can push off with triple-barrel. **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluffs vs line 1. FOLD to multi-street aggression. Triple-barrel passive calling mode.

**Player 6**: **Tight raiser (~9%), wide limper/caller. BIGGEST LOSER this session (lost ~half stack).** 3-bets = QQ+/AK. Cold 4-bets = AA/KK. Donk-bets wide including underpairs. Extremely sticky on dry boards but barrels medium-strength (second pair) and may check back river. **KEY WEAKNESS**: Folds QQ/KK on ace-high boards. Folds to sustained double-barrels. **Exploit**: Fold to 3-bets/4-bets. Isolate limps freely. Bluff ace-high boards and scary turns. Double-barrel with range advantage. Call down lighter vs barrels (overvalues medium pairs). Don't bluff dry boards.

**Player 7**: **Wider than TAG — calls broadways and wide from blinds.** Passive preflop, AGGRESSIVE postflop — donk-leads and double-barrels with strength. Raises flop with just top pair on paired boards (spewy). Once committed, calls down with one pair on scary boards. **Exploit**: Value bet relentlessly when ahead. Flop raises often = just top pair. Don't bluff once they've shown aggression. Respect donk-lead + double-barrel combos.

## My Table Image & Discipline

**Image after 2 sessions**: Very tight — actual VPIP ~15% last session (3/20 hands played). All three wins were fold equity plays (opponents folded). Image is HIGHLY credible for steals and bluffs. Opponents will respect my bets/raises.

**Image leverage**: Can profitably open wider from steal positions and semi-bluff more — opponents are folding to my aggression. Should selectively exploit this before image adjusts.

**Biggest historical leak: Medium-strength hands.** A8o-ATo and mid pairs (77) generate largest losses. Hand 4 loss with AdTs (-$75) reinforces this. Premium hands and steals are profitable.

**Leaks to avoid**: (1) Playing/continuing with weak aces (A8o-ATo type) in raised pots without clear edge. (2) Investing with mid pairs then folding. (3) Calling flop bets with just overcards vs sticky players.

## Core Strategy

1. **VPIP target: 20-25%.** Last session's ~15% was disciplined but potentially too tight — all profits came from fold equity, zero showdowns. Slightly widen to capture more value while maintaining tight image.
2. **Hand selection**: Premiums (TT+, AJ+, KQ) for value. Suited connectors/small pairs only in position vs limpers. ATs+ from steal positions. FOLD weak aces and offsuit broadways below AJ.
3. **Leverage tight image**: Open wider from CO/BTN when blinds are weak players. Use image for semi-bluffs on scare cards.
4. **Against stations (P2, P4, P7)**: Value bet wide, NEVER bluff, isolate limps.
5. **Against P5 (nit)**: Two-barrel bluff single donk-bets. FOLD to multi-street aggression. Triple-barrel passive mode.
6. **Against P6**: Bluff ace-high/scary boards. Double-barrel. Fold to preflop aggression. Call barrels lighter.
7. **Against P3 (skilled)**: Tighten steals. Don't thin value-bet rivers (traps). Respect 4-bets but can call wider.
8. **Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled) > P2 (LAG volume) > P4 (station accumulator) > P7 (spewy aggression) > P6 (exploitable) > P5 (predictable nit).

**Opponent Profiles (Session-Refined & Confirmed)**

- **Player 1 – Loose-Leaning TAG (River Honest):**  
  Defends wider preflop and will float when sensing weakness, but large river aggression remains value-heavy.  
  → Apply turn pressure on coordinated boards.  
  → Thin value early streets.  
  → Fold bluff-catchers versus strong river lines.

- **Player 3 – Passive Value-Trapper:**  
  Flats strong hands preflop; prefers call-down lines with strong but non-nut holdings. Rarely bluff-raises.  
  → Do not over-barrel into condensed ranges.  
  → When he raises turn/river, heavily value-weighted.  
  → Can value-own himself by under-raising strong hands — size value bets confidently but avoid triple-barrel spew.

- **Player 4 – True LAG / Structural Pressure:**  
  Most capable of applying multi-street aggression and attacking capped ranges.  
  → Strengthen value 3-bets and 4-bets.

  → Reduce marginal bluff-catching in big pots.

- **Player 5 – Tight TAG, Initiative = Strength:**  
  Conservative preflop, aggression skews value postflop (including donk leads).  
  → Steal frequently.  
  → Overfold to strong multi-street lines.  
  → Respect donk/turn aggression.

- **Player 6 – Loose-Aggressive, Two-Street Player:**  
  Wide preflop. C-bets and double-barrels medium-strength hands. River aggression more capped and honest.  
  → Defend wider in position.  
  → Do not over-fold to turn barrels.  
  → Attack river checks after double barrels.  
  → River bets remain value-heavy.

  Strength-heavy across all streets.  
  → Steal relentlessly.  
  → No big bluffs; fold to strong aggression.

Opens extremely wide, calls 3-bets light (A8o-type hands), and floats flops with high-card hands. **Barrels turns aggressively but will check turns on scare cards (A-high, completing draws). Bets rivers aggressively when checked to on safe runouts (paired boards, blanks), representing strength.** Exploit by 3-betting wide for value, applying pressure when they show passivity, and never bluffing rivers after they check.

- Player 2: EXTREME LAG when opening, but becomes straightforward and sticky when calling raises. **Calls down with marginal made hands that have potential, reluctant to fold once invested.** Donk-bets flops in raised AND 3-bet pots but folds to any raise. In limped pots, plays draws passively but bets made hands aggressively. **Slow-plays strong hands (two pair+) on all streets in single-raised pots, not just river.** Check-calling multiple streets often indicates monster hands rather than draws.

- Player 4: Elite TAG - primary threat at table. **3-bets with premium range; calls 3-bets with stronger-than-average but not premium range (Ax, pairs, broadways).** In 3-bet pots where THEY are the aggressor, leads flops aggressively with large sizings when board favors their range and continues with heavy turn pressure. **When they CALL a 3-bet, play more fit-or-fold and will fold to flop pressure on scary/coordinated boards.** In single-raised pots, plays more passively and can be pushed off marginal holdings on later streets. When they show aggression, especially multi-way, their range is extremely strong - fold all marginal hands.

- Player 5: LAG with both preflop and postflop aggression. 3-bets with strong, polarized range (not just a caller). When they just call preflop, they become aggressive postflop with donk-bets and turn barrels, **but also show call-down tendencies and can fold to river pressure.** When they 3-bet preflop, they show continued aggression on later streets. Exploit by respecting their 3-bets, but attacking their postflop aggression when they flat preflop. Their multi-street commitment is real strength, not bluff-heavy, **but they can be pushed off marginal holdings on the river.**

- Player 6: Tight 3-bettor (QQ+, AK) but **opens wider than premium hands in single-raised pots (A9o-type hands). Capable of triple-barreling with marginal pairs in single-raised pots when they have initiative.** As caller in 3-bet pots, leads flops but folds to turn pressure when facing aggression. Straightforward postflop - folds when board misses their range. Exploit by folding to their 3-bets without premium holdings, applying pressure on unfavorable boards, **but respect their multi-street aggression in single-raised pots and target them in 3-bet pots when they are the caller.**

- **3-bet pot dynamics are opponent-specific and position-dependent: value bet thinner against stations (Player 1, 3), but respect aggression from tight players (Player 4, 6) AND from LAGs who 3-bet preflop (Player 5). Target Player 6 specifically when they are caller (not aggressor) in 3-bet pots.**
- When facing flop leads in 3-bet pots from TAG players, especially multi-way, treat as extreme strength.
- Player 5's 3-bet range is strong and continues postflop. When they flat preflop, their postflop aggression is more exploitable.
- **Scare cards on turn (A-high, completing draws) can slow LAGs down, but they often fire rivers on safe runouts. Don't assume shutdown after turn check.**

SELF-IMAGE & ADJUSTMENTS:
- Table image: Extremely tight (folded 70% of hands). This is profitable but creates exploitation opportunity. Plan: Begin mixing in selective 3-bet bluffs and river raises against thinking opponents who respect my tight image, particularly targeting Players 1 and 2.
- Continue selective hand selection but increase aggression factor when entering pots to balance image.
- Primary leak to address: Stop bleeding chips with marginal broadway hands (KQ, KJ, QJ) in raised pots without clear initiative. These hands perform poorly against the calling/3-betting ranges of Players 1, 3, and 4.

- **Player 2** is a confirmed **LAG (VPIP ~50%, PFR ~30%)** who calls wide preflop, including from the blinds, but folds too often to early aggression on dry, static boards when out of position. However, across 20 hands, they consistently **call multiple streets with marginal made hands**—especially **second pair, bottom two pair, or backdoor pair-plus combos**—when the board pairs or connects partially with their range. **Exploit**: C-bet dry flops aggressively, but **avoid over-bluffing on paired turns/rivers**. Value bet thinner on early streets, but **reserve triple-barrels for strong hands or when holding clear blockers** to their likely two-pair combinations.

- **Player 3** is **not a standard TAG**. Despite modest VPIP/PFR stats, they **call raises from early position with hands like ATo** and **continue with top two pair across three streets**, indicating a **wider and more resilient range than typical tight players**. They likely fall into a **semi-LAG or loose TAG** category, especially on broadway-heavy boards. **Exploit**: **Widen their estimated calling/continuation ranges**, particularly on A/K-high boards. **Assume they can call down with second pair or top two**, so **avoid overcommitting with marginal top pair (e.g., KJ on A-high)**.

- **Player 5** remains a **tight-passive player (VPIP ~33%, PFR ~11%)** who limps and folds to raises, but **calls multiple streets with medium-strength hands** when they connect. No evidence of bluff-calling or overfolding postflop. **Exploit unchanged**: **Value bet thin on dynamic boards**, **avoid turn bluffs**, and **consider checking back marginal value** to control pot size.

- **Your table image** is **tight-aggressive**, which continues to generate preflop and flop folds. However, this session exposed a **tendency to overvalue marginal top pair (e.g., KJ, AT) on A/K-high boards**, especially when facing calls from tight or semi-tight players. Against opponents who **call multiple streets with strong-but-not-nutted hands**, **triple-barreling with second-kicker top pair is often unprofitable**. **Strategic adjustment**: On **A/K-high boards**, **check back the turn with marginal top pair** when the river is likely to brick—**preserving chips is more valuable than forcing thin value**.

- **Board texture awareness refined**: **Dry, static boards remain high-fold-frequency spots on the flop**, but **paired boards—especially when the turn pairs a non-flop card—dramatically increase the likelihood that LAGs have improved to two pair or better**. **C-bet dry flops liberally**, but **proceed with extreme caution on paired turns/rivers**. **Strong two pair or better should bet for value**, but **marginal two pair (e.g., bottom + middle) should often check against LAGs who call wide**.

- **Overall session takeaway**: **Winning small pots with aggression is effective**, but **losing big pots with marginal top pair against tight/semi-tight callers is the primary leak**. **Focus on hand-vs-range accuracy on later streets**, especially when your hand is vulnerable to better kickers or sets. **Fold more often on turns/rivers when your top pair is second-best by kicker and your opponent shows consistent strength**.
